newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Plans for 3rd Irish TV channel receives setback.
newsitem.headline: Plans for 3rd Irish TV channel receives setback.

text.p: Plans for a third television channel in Ireland suffered a severe setback on Wednesday when a key shareholder, Northern Ireland's Ulster Television Plc, announced it was pulling out of a TV3 consortium.

UTV said in a results statement that it was withdrawing from the consortium because it had not been able to reach agreement with Ireland's Independent Radio and Television Commission (IRTC) on certain issues.

The TV3 consortium earlier issued a separate statement saying the primary areas of concern had been over the level of control held by UTV and the extent to which the association of UTV and TV3 might lead to distortions in the market place.
The TV3 consortium said the overall viability of the project to add a third, independent channel was not in question.
A spokesman for the consortium said it had no further comment until it received new information. UTV, Northern Ireland's independent news and entertainment channel, was not available for comment.

UTV, which announced its participation in a TV3 consortium last September, was understood to have committed itself to taking a 40 percent stake worth approximately six million pounds sterling ($9.4 million), making it the largest single shareholder.
UTV was seen as a key player in the operation because it would have brough programme-making and technical expertise to the fledgling channel.
In its results statement UTV said the group had submitted a business plan to the IRTC but some of the terms of the UTV/TV3 agreement were unacceptable to the IRTC.

"Our board feels that the risks associated with proceeding with the proposal on the terms required by the IRTC would not be in the interests of either the company or the shareholders," UTV said in the statement.

A further one third of the shareholding was expected to be made available to institutional investors, with the rest of the equity held by the manager of Irish rock band U2, Paul McGuinness, James Morris of Windmill Lane Studios and accountant Ossie Kilkenny.
The group had been awarded the exclusive right to negotiate over the granting of a television programme service contract for a new national independent television channel in Ireland.
Semi-state company RTE currently holds the monopoly on the Republic's two existing channels RTE 1 and Network 2.
